description: Ground truth for the dedicated validation/dataflow golden corpus (Phase 6 of the Analysis Correctness & Dataflow Verification spec; extended for the Dataflow Correctness, Symbol Resolution & Cross-Layer Evidence spec's Golden Corpus phase). Each entry is a finding that SHOULD be produced when this corpus is analyzed with contract.json loaded via --contracts; any produced finding not listed here counts as a false positive. Covers the 16 originally required test groups (see the per-file comments in corpus/*.ts for which group each case belongs to): correct validation, missing validation, unused validator, result-ignored/raw-reuse-after-validation, validation in a separate never-called function, cross-function handoffs (both a validated-and-traced good path and a raw-and-unflagged-otherwise bad path), multiple .max() merging, multiple format AND-merging, an unresolvable Zod modifier, an AST-verified alias validator, a generic exception unrelated to the request, mass assignment via spread, security requirements Stoa cannot verify (must produce NOTHING), and conflicting FE/BE implementations under one trace ID. Every z.object() schema in this corpus (01, 02, 04, 05) correctly matches its one contract-named field, so none of them produce a shape-level R-VALIDATION-CONTRACT-UNRESOLVED finding (field-by-field z.object() resolution, added after this corpus first caught every such schema as a false 'unresolved') — only 03's .refine()-modified field, which genuinely is not a recognized scalar chain, still does. 07-symbol-and-shape.ts adds four more representative groups: symbol-based shadowing (a shadowed, differently-shaped `result` in a nested block must NOT reach repo.save() — correctly produces NOTHING), safeParse() used without a proven success check (SAFEPARSE-UNGUARDED), an object-field conflict where FE/BE z.object() schemas share one trace ID but disagree on the contract-named field's minimum (CONFLICT, same mechanism as group 16 but via field-by-field object resolution instead of two scalar schemas), a field literally named "constructor" that must still resolve via Object.hasOwn() and match its contract entry (correctly produces NOTHING, proving the prototype-safety fix), and a nested z.object() field that is not a recognized scalar chain and correctly stays UNRESOLVED rather than being guessed at.
